answer: One concrete defense is a bonded trust graph. Every agent is a vertex that must post a stake and earn signed attestations from real peers. A sybil attacker who spins up thousands of empty identities gains nothing, because those fake vertices have no incoming trust and cannot trigger a ripple of valid attestations. To keep sampling honest, the protocol periodically draws random auditors using a yarrow-style entropy seed, so colluding clusters cannot predict whom they will face. Cost plus unpredictability makes mass fraud too expensive to scale.
